question: The first volume of 'Akbar Nama' focuses on which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar's ancestors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Akbarnama (अकबरनामा) is the official chronicle of the reign of Emperor Akbar, written by his court historian Abul Fazl in Persian.

• It is divided into three volumes; the first volume deals with the history of Akbar's ancestors — from Timur down to Humayun — and the birth of Akbar.

• The second volume records the events of Akbar's reign, and the third volume, the Ain-i-Akbari, describes the administration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Abul Fazl was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court.

• The work was commissioned by Akbar himself and took about seven years to complete.

• Beautifully illustrated manuscripts of the Akbarnama are preserved in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

NOTE

• Akbar's administration (Option 1): This is the subject of the third volume, the Ain-i-Akbari, not the first volume.

• Events of Akbar's reign (Option 2): These form the content of the second volume of the Akbarnama.

• Geography of the Mughal Empire (Option 3): The Akbarnama is a historical chronicle, not a work devoted to geography of the empire.

question: Which Mughal emperor led a campaign against Kashmir, and in which year did it took place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar, 1586.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mughal Emperor Akbar (अकबर) annexed Kashmir in 1586 after sending an expedition led by his generals.

• Kashmir was ruled by the Chak dynasty (Yusuf Shah Chak) at the time, and it was incorporated as a suba (province) of the Mughal Empire.

• The conquest gave the Mughals control over the strategic and scenic Kashmir valley.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Akbar visited Kashmir several times and admired its beauty.

• Under the Mughals, Kashmir became famous for its gardens such as the Shalimar and Nishat Bagh (built later under Jahangir and Shah Jahan).

• Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605 and greatly expanded the empire.

NOTE

• Babur, 1531 (Option 1): Babur died in 1530; he founded the Mughal Empire in 1526 after the First Battle of Panipat but did not conquer Kashmir.

• Humayun, 1538 (Option 2): Humayun was struggling against Sher Shah Suri around this time and lost his empire, not linked to a Kashmir campaign.

• Jahangir, 1617 (Option 3): Jahangir loved Kashmir and developed its gardens, but the region was already annexed earlier by Akbar.

question: Which committee recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Balwant Rai Mehta Committee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (बलवंत राय मेहता समिति), appointed in 1957, recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

• The three tiers are Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.

• Rajasthan was the first state to implement Panchayati Raj (at Nagaur) on 2 October 1959.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Panchayati Raj was given constitutional status by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

• Panchayati Raj is a subject under the State List and the Directive Principles (Article 40).

• The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.

NOTE

• Ashok Mehta Committee (Option 1): Set up in 1977, it recommended a two-tier system (Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat).

• GVK Rao Committee (Option 3): Appointed in 1985, it recommended strengthening the district-level planning and the Zila Parishad.

• L M Singhvi Committee (Option 4): Formed in 1986, it recommended constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj institutions.

question: The report of _____ member Justice Hema Committee, formed in 2017 was released in 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Justice Hema Committee (न्यायमूर्ति हेमा समिति) was a three-member committee constituted by the Kerala government in 2017.

• It was formed to study the issues, gender inequality and problems faced by women in the Malayalam film industry.

• The committee's report was finally made public in 2024, exposing widespread harassment and exploitation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The committee was headed by retired High Court judge Justice K. Hema.

• It was set up in the wake of the 2017 actress assault case and demands by the Women in Cinema Collective (WCC).

• The report triggered major discussion on workplace safety for women in cinema.

NOTE

• 1 (Option 1): An incorrect figure; the committee was not a single-member body.

• 5 (Option 3): Not correct; the committee had three members, not five.

• 7 (Option 4): Incorrect; there were only three members in the Justice Hema Committee.

question: Smart Cities Mission in June 2025 completed how many years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Smart Cities Mission (स्मार्ट सिटीज मिशन) was launched on 25 June 2015, so in June 2025 it completed 10 years.

• It is a flagship urban development programme of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

• The mission aims to promote cities that provide core infrastructure, a clean environment and a decent quality of life through 'smart' solutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A total of 100 cities were selected under the Mission through a competition-based process.

• Key focus areas include e-governance, smart mobility, water and waste management, and area-based development.

• The Mission works largely through Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) in each city.

NOTE

• 8 (Option 2): Would correspond to a 2017 launch, which is incorrect.

• 9 (Option 3): Would correspond to a 2016 launch, which is incorrect.

• 7 (Option 4): Would correspond to a 2018 launch, which is incorrect.

question: As per the Henley Passport Index 2025, what is India's rank in passport strength?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 77th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Henley Passport Index 2025 (हेनले पासपोर्ट सूचकांक), India was ranked 77th in passport strength.

• India climbed up the rankings, with visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to around 59 destinations.

• The Henley Passport Index ranks passports by the number of destinations their holders can access without a prior visa.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The index is compiled by Henley & Partners using data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

• Singapore topped the 2025 index as the world's most powerful passport.

• The index is updated periodically through the year.

NOTE

• 65th (Option 2): Not India's 2025 rank on the Henley Passport Index.

• 75th (Option 3): An incorrect ranking figure for India in 2025.

• 90th (Option 4): Does not match India's 77th position in the 2025 index.

question: How many countries were ranked in the World Press Freedom Index 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 180.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The World Press Freedom Index 2025 (वर्ल्ड प्रेस फ्रीडम सूचकांक) ranked a total of 180 countries and territories.

• The index is published annually by Reporters Without Borders (RSF / Reporters Sans Frontières).

• It assesses press freedom based on political, economic, legislative, social and safety indicators.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India was ranked 151st in the 2025 index.

• Norway has consistently topped the index in recent years.

• The index is released around World Press Freedom Day (3 May).

NOTE

• 150 (Option 2): Not the number of countries assessed; the index covers 180.

• 200 (Option 3): Exceeds the number of countries actually ranked in the index.

• 132 (Option 4): Incorrect; the index consistently ranks 180 nations.

question:
Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of Export Preparedness Index of India?
I. Export policy
II. Business environment
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Export Preparedness Index (निर्यात तैयारी सूचकांक) of India is prepared by NITI Aayog.

• Its four pillars are Policy, Business Ecosystem, Export Ecosystem and Export Performance — which include both 'Export policy' and 'Business environment'.

• Since both statements I and II ARE pillars, the correct choice for the one that is NOT a pillar is Neither I nor II.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The index measures the export preparedness and performance of Indian states and UTs.

• It identifies challenges and opportunities to strengthen India's export potential.

• The pillars are further divided into several sub-pillars.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because 'Export policy' IS a pillar of the index.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because 'Business environment' IS a pillar of the index.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since both are genuine pillars, neither is the odd one out.

question: The Flamingo Festival 2025 was conducted in _____ from January 18 to 20.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tirupati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Flamingo Festival 2025 (फ्लेमिंगो महोत्सव) was held in the Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh from 18 to 20 January 2025.

• It is celebrated to promote tourism at the Pulicat Lake and Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary.

• The festival showcases the migratory flamingos and other birds that flock to the region.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pulicat Lake is the second largest brackish water lagoon in India after Chilika Lake.

• Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary is one of the largest pelican habitats in Southeast Asia.

• The festival supports eco-tourism and awareness about bird conservation.

NOTE

• Patna (Option 1): Capital of Bihar; not the venue of the Flamingo Festival.

• Shimla (Option 3): A Himalayan hill station in Himachal Pradesh, unrelated to the festival.

• Chandigarh (Option 4): A Union Territory and capital of Punjab and Haryana, not the venue.

question: The Government of India has set a target of achieving 140 GW of wind power capacity by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2030.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has set a target of achieving 140 GW of wind power capacity (पवन ऊर्जा क्षमता) by 2030.

• This is part of India's larger goal of 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel energy capacity by 2030.

• Wind energy is a key component of India's renewable energy and climate commitments.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India is among the top countries in the world in installed wind power capacity.

• Tamil Nadu and Gujarat are leading states in wind energy generation.

• The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) oversees wind power development.

NOTE

• 2026 (Option 1): Too early for the 140 GW target; not the stated year.

• 2027 (Option 2): Not the government's target year for 140 GW of wind power.

• 2050 (Option 4): Relates to India's net-zero emissions goal, not the 140 GW wind target.

question: Geostationary orbit satellites travel at about _____ km per second.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Satellites in the geostationary orbit (भूस्थिर कक्षा) travel at about 3 km per second (roughly 3.07 km/s).

• A geostationary orbit lies at an altitude of about 35,786 km above the equator.

• The satellite completes one revolution in 24 hours, matching Earth's rotation, so it appears stationary from the ground.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Geostationary satellites are widely used for communication, weather forecasting and broadcasting.

• The concept of geostationary orbit was popularised by writer Arthur C. Clarke.

• India's INSAT and GSAT series operate in geostationary orbit.

NOTE

• 15 (Option 1): Far too high; low-Earth-orbit velocities are around 7-8 km/s, not 15.

• 10 (Option 2): Higher than any typical satellite orbital speed; incorrect.

• 25 (Option 3): Unrealistically high for a satellite; closer to some interplanetary escape speeds.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding force?
I. If an unbalanced force is applied on the object, there will be a change either in its speed or in the direction of its motion.
II. To accelerate the motion of an object, a balanced force is required.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An unbalanced force (असंतुलित बल) acting on an object changes its speed or direction of motion, so statement I is correct.

• To accelerate an object, an unbalanced (net) force is needed, not a balanced force — so statement II is incorrect.

• A balanced force produces no acceleration; the object stays at rest or moves with uniform velocity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This is based on Newton's First and Second Laws of Motion.

• Newton's second law states F = ma; acceleration requires a net (unbalanced) force.

• When forces are balanced, the net force is zero and there is no change in the state of motion.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because a balanced force cannot cause acceleration.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, since statement II is false.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Wrong, since statement I is true.

question: From which island did DRDO conduct the 'Pralay' missile tests in July 2025?
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The DRDO conducted the 'Pralay' (प्रलय) short-range ballistic missile tests in July 2025 from Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast.

• This island, earlier known as Wheeler Island, is India's principal missile testing range.

• Pralay is a surface-to-surface, quasi-ballistic missile with a range of about 150-500 km.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The island was renamed in 2015 in honour of former President and 'Missile Man' Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

• It hosts the Integrated Test Range (ITR) of the DRDO.

• Pralay is designed to be difficult to intercept due to its manoeuvrable trajectory.

NOTE

• Nicobar Islands (Option 1): Part of the Andaman and Nicobar group; not the missile test site.

• Lakshadweep island (Option 2): An Arabian Sea archipelago, not a DRDO missile range.

• Andaman Islands (Option 3): A Bay of Bengal group; the tests were off the Odisha coast, not here.

question: Which Mughal emperor ruled between 1713 and 1719?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Farrukh Siyar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Farrukh Siyar (फर्रुखसियर) was the Mughal emperor who ruled from 1713 to 1719.

• He ascended the throne with the help of the powerful Sayyid Brothers (Abdullah Khan and Hussain Ali Khan).

• He was later blinded and killed by the same Sayyid Brothers in 1719.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In 1717, Farrukh Siyar issued a farman granting the English East India Company duty-free trading rights in Bengal — often called the 'Magna Carta' of the Company.

• His reign marks the era of the declining and increasingly puppet Mughal emperors.

• The Sayyid Brothers were known as the 'king-makers' of the later Mughal period.

NOTE

• Ahmad Shah (Option 1): A later Mughal emperor who ruled from 1748 to 1754.

• Shah Alam II (Option 3): Ruled from 1759 to 1806; associated with the Battle of Buxar.

• Alamgir II (Option 4): Ruled from 1754 to 1759, after Ahmad Shah.

question: Which military strategy did Shivaji often use against his opponents?
option_2: Warfare with the help of elephant
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guerrilla warfare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhatrapati Shivaji often used guerrilla warfare (गुरिल्ला युद्धकला), known in Marathi as Ganimi Kava.

• This involved swift surprise attacks, ambushes and rapid retreats, using the hilly Deccan terrain to advantage.

• The tactic helped his smaller Maratha forces defeat larger Mughal and Adil Shahi armies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shivaji founded the Maratha Empire and was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674.

• He built a strong network of hill forts and a notable navy.

• His administration was guided by a council of ministers called the Ashta Pradhan.

NOTE

• Open field battle (Option 1): Not Shivaji's preferred method, as his forces were smaller and lightly armed.

• Warfare with the help of elephant (Option 2): Elephants were more typical of Mughal and Rajput armies, not Maratha guerrilla tactics.

• Siege tactics (Option 4): While Shivaji captured forts, his signature strategy was mobile guerrilla warfare, not prolonged sieges.

question: The NSE introduced trading in Index Options (also based on Nifty 50) on June 4, _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2001.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Stock Exchange (NSE / एन.एस.ई.) introduced trading in Index Options based on the Nifty 50 on June 4, 2001.

• This was part of the introduction of derivatives trading in the Indian securities market.

• Index futures had been launched a year earlier, in June 2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The NSE was established in 1992 and began operations in 1994.

• Its benchmark index is the Nifty 50, comprising 50 large companies.

• Stock options on individual securities were introduced in July 2001.

NOTE

• 2006 (Option 1): Later than the actual launch year of index options on the NSE.

• 2003 (Option 3): Incorrect; index options were already trading since 2001.

• 2005 (Option 4): Does not match the June 2001 launch of index options.

question: The Hill area development programme was initiated during the _____th five-year plan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hill Area Development Programme (पहाड़ी क्षेत्र विकास कार्यक्रम) was initiated during the Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79).

• It aimed at the socio-economic development of designated hill areas and their people.

• The programme focused on eco-preservation, horticulture, and improving livelihoods in hilly regions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Related programmes like the Tribal Area Development Programme were also emphasised in the Fifth Plan.

• The Fifth Plan focused on 'Garibi Hatao' (removal of poverty) and self-reliance.

• Hill Area Development covers areas such as parts of Uttarakhand, Assam, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.

NOTE

• 10 (Option 1): The Tenth Plan (2002-07) is far later than the programme's initiation.

• 8 (Option 2): The Eighth Plan (1992-97) did not start this programme.

• 7 (Option 4): The Seventh Plan (1985-90) is after the actual initiation in the Fifth Plan.

question: The AGMARK is the certification mark for _____ in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is agriculture products.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• AGMARK (कृषि उत्पाद प्रमाणन) is a certification mark for agricultural products in India, assuring their quality.

• It is governed by the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937 (amended 1986).

• The mark is administered by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) under the Ministry of Agriculture.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• AGMARK covers products such as pulses, cereals, spices, honey, edible oils and ghee.

• The word AGMARK is derived from 'Agricultural Marketing'.

• The DMI has its headquarters at Faridabad.

NOTE

• Industrial products (Option 1): Standardised under ISI/BIS, not AGMARK.

• Software products (Option 2): Not covered by AGMARK, which is for agricultural produce.

• Financial products (Option 4): Regulated by bodies like RBI and SEBI, not by AGMARK.

question: The first complete census of an Indian city was conducted in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1830.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first complete census of an Indian city (भारतीय शहर की पहली पूर्ण जनगणना) was conducted in 1830.

• It was carried out by Henry Walter in the city of Dacca (Dhaka).

• This was one of the earliest systematic population counts of an urban area in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first synchronous (simultaneous) census of India was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

• The first non-synchronous census was attempted in 1872 under Lord Mayo.

• Since 1881, the census in India has been conducted every ten years (decennial).

NOTE

• 1810 (Option 2): Too early; no complete city census had yet been conducted in India.

• 1840 (Option 3): Later than the actual first complete city census of 1830.

• 1820 (Option 4): Incorrect; the first complete city census took place in 1830, not 1820.

question:
In India, Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 was conducted by which of the following?
I. Ministry of Rural Development
II. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 (सामाजिक-आर्थिक एवं जाति जनगणना) was conducted in two parts — rural and urban.

• The rural component was carried out by the Ministry of Rural Development, and the urban component by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

• Hence both ministries were involved in conducting the SECC 2011.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• SECC 2011 was the first caste-based census since 1931.

• It provides data used for identifying beneficiaries of government welfare schemes.

• The Registrar General of India assisted in the process.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as the urban part was handled by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as the rural part was handled by the Ministry of Rural Development.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both ministries were indeed involved.

question: During British rule in India, caste data was regularly collected in decennial censuses from 1881 to _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1931.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During British rule, caste data (जाति संबंधी आंकड़े) was regularly collected in the decennial censuses from 1881 to 1931.

• The 1931 census was the last one to record comprehensive caste-wise data.

• The 1941 census data on caste was not fully compiled or published due to the Second World War.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• After independence, caste enumeration (except SC/ST) was discontinued in the general census.

• The 1931 census is still often cited as a reference for caste proportions in India.

• The first synchronous census in India was held in 1881.

NOTE

• 1921 (Option 1): Caste data collection continued beyond this year up to 1931.

• 1911 (Option 2): An intermediate census year; not the last one to record caste data.

• 1901 (Option 4): Too early; regular caste enumeration continued until 1931.

question: Which of the following has amalgamated a large number of central and state taxes and cesses?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goods and Services Tax.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Goods and Services Tax (वस्तु एवं सेवा कर) amalgamated a large number of central and state taxes and cesses into a single tax.

• It subsumed taxes such as excise duty, service tax, VAT, entertainment tax and octroi.

• GST was implemented in India on 1 July 2017 through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• GST is a destination-based, multi-stage, value-added tax on the supply of goods and services.

• It is administered by the GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

• GST has four main slabs: 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%.

NOTE

• Customs duty (Option 2): A tax on imports and exports; it was not subsumed into GST.

• Minimum Alternate tax (Option 3): A tax under the Income Tax Act on companies; a direct tax, not part of GST.

• Corporate tax (Option 4): A direct tax on company profits; not merged into GST.

question: Which ancient Sanskrit grammarian lived during the time of the Nandas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Panini.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Panini (पाणिनि) was an ancient Sanskrit grammarian traditionally associated with the era of the Nanda dynasty.

• He authored the famous grammar treatise 'Ashtadhyayi', one of the earliest works on linguistics.

• He is regarded as the 'Father of Sanskrit Grammar' and belonged to the region of Gandhara (Shalatula).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ashtadhyayi contains around 4,000 rules (sutras) systematising Sanskrit grammar.

• Panini's work influenced later grammarians such as Katyayana and Patanjali.

• His analysis of language is admired even by modern linguists.

NOTE

• Kalidasa (Option 1): A great Sanskrit poet and dramatist of the Gupta era, author of Abhijnanashakuntalam, not a grammarian of the Nanda period.

• Aryabhata (Option 2): A mathematician and astronomer of the Gupta age, author of the Aryabhatiya.

• Patanjali (Option 4): A later grammarian (author of the Mahabhashya) and the Yoga Sutras, of the Shunga period, not the Nanda era.

question: Who are traditionally believed to have composed the Vedic hymns in early Indian tradition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rishis and Rishikas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In early Indian tradition, the Vedic hymns (वैदिक भजन) are traditionally believed to have been composed by Rishis (sages) and Rishikas (female sages).

• These seers are said to have 'seen' or 'received' the hymns, which were passed down orally through generations.

• Female sages such as Lopamudra, Ghosha, Gargi and Maitreyi are associated with the Vedic tradition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and contains hymns to various deities.

• The Vedic hymns were preserved through the oral (Shruti) tradition.

• Each Veda has Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads.

NOTE

• Kings (Option 1): Kings were patrons and performers of rituals but are not credited with composing the hymns.

• Scholars from Nalanda (Option 2): Nalanda was a much later Buddhist university (c. 5th century CE), long after the Vedic hymns.

• Village elders (Option 3): They did not compose the Vedic hymns, which are attributed to the Rishis and Rishikas.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct?
I. During the Vedic period the society was organised into four varnas.
II. Early Hindu philosophy prescribed the four stages of life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the Vedic period, society was organised into four varnas (चार वर्ण) — Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras — so statement I is correct.

• Early Hindu philosophy also prescribed the four stages of life (ashramas) — Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sanyasa — so statement II is correct.

• Together, this system is known as the Varnashrama Dharma.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Purusha Sukta of the Rigveda is often cited in connection with the origin of the four varnas.

• The four ashramas represent the ideal stages of human life based on age and duty.

• The four Purusharthas (goals of life) are Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as statement II about the four ashramas is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as statement I about the four varnas is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are true.
